State vs Ajay Kumar on 7 February, 2024 
 In The Court Of Ms. Neha Gupta Singh, Chief
 Metropolitan Magistrate : North District :
 Delhi
State Vs. : Ajay Kumar
Fir No : 185/2018
P. S. : Alipur
U/s : 279/304A Ipc
 Judgment
 (a) Serial No. of the 2434/2019  case  (b) Date of offence 21.04.2018  (c) Complainant ASI Virender  (d) Accused Ajay Kumar  S/o Chand Ram  R/o Village Shershah, Dist. Sonipat,
 Haryana  (e) Offence U/Sec. 279/304A IPC  (f) Plea of accused Pleaded not guilty  (g) Final Order Acquittal  (h) Date of institution 03.05.2019  ( i) Date of reserve of 07.02.2024  order / judgment  (j) Date of judgment 07.02.2024 BRIEF STATEMENT OF FACTS FOR THE DECISION:-
1. The prosecution story in brief is that on 21.04.2018 at about 07.08 a.m., near Singhu village Toll Tax, village Singhu, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS Alipur, accused was found driving a car bearing registration no. DL-8CAR-2481 in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others. It is further alleged that while driving the aforesaid vehicle in aforesaid manner, accused hit against one motorcycle CT-100 which resulted in death of the occupant of the motorcycle namely, Joginder. 
2. Investigation was completed and police report under section 173 Cr.P.C. was filed under sections 279304A IPC. Cognizance was taken and accused was summoned. 
3. Copy of charge sheet and documents were supplied to the accused in compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C.
State vs Ajay Kumar on 7 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19921233/
1 4. Arguments on notice were heard and notice against accused Ajay Kumar was framed under section 279/304A IPC by Ld. Predecessor vide order dated 07.08.2019. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 
5. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused prosecution examined only four witness. 
6. PW1 Abhishek deposed that on 21.04.2018 at about 7.00 p.m. when he was going to Kundli,
Sonipat through Singhu toll road and reached at Singhu village, toll tax booth, one martui swift car came from behind in rash and negligent manner and crossed him and hit against one motorcycle which was coming from his opposite side due to impact of hitting motorcyclist fell down on the road. 
He further deposed that meanwhile he also reached at the spot and 2-3 persons came out from the said car and took the injured to the hospital. 
The said witness was declared hostile by the Ld. APP for the State and was cross-examined but nothing incriminating has come on record. Ld. Defence counsel for accused has not cross-examined the said witness despite being given opportunity to him. 
7. PW-2 Sh. Rahul deposed that he was doing the courier work in Amazon company. He deposed the same facts as alleged by PW-1 Abhishek. Thus, there is no need to reproduced the same. 
The said witness was declared hostile by the Ld. APP for the State and was cross-examined but nothing incriminating has come on record. Ld. Defence counsel for accused has not cross-examined the said witness despite being given opportunity to him. 
8. PW-3 Neeraj deposed that he was doing the Govt. job in FCI. On 21.04.2018 he alongwith his friend Ajay was going to Sonipat from Delhi and when they reached at Singhu Border Toll Road,
they have seen public persons gathered at the spot. He further deposed that at the request of public persons and police officials they shifted the injured to SRHC Hospital and after admitting the injured in the hospital, he left for his house. He further deposed that on 30.04.2018 he was called by the police officials of Alipur and inquired from him about the incident. He has not seen the car no.
or the driver of the offending vehicle. 
The said witness was declared hostile by the Ld. APP for the State and was cross-examined but nothing incriminating has come on record. Ld. Defence counsel for accused has not cross-examined the said witness despite being given opportunity to him. 
9. PW-4 Sh. Sumer Singh deposed that he is the registered owner of the vehicle no. DL-8C-AR-2481. 
In the year 2018, he was called by the police officials of PS Alipur. He came to the PS Alipur and handed over his aforesaid vehicle to police officials as they said that his vehicle is involved in an accident case. Thereafter he got released his aforesaid vehicle on superdari vide superdariname Ex.
PW-4/A. Ld. Defence counsel for accused has not cross-examined the said witness despite being given opportunity to him State vs Ajay Kumar on 7 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19921233/
2 10. PW-1 Abhishek and PW-2 Rahul, eye witnesses and PW- 3 Neeraj, injured who are the main witnesses in the present case have turned hostile. They have not supported the version of the prosecution. All other witnesses are formal witnesses, examining them would have been a futile exercise. Accordingly PE was closed. Statement U/s 313 Cr.P.C. is dispensed with as no incriminating evidence has come on record. Final arguments were heard. 
11. I have heard the arguments addressed by the Learned APP Sh. Gurdaulat Singh Sidhu for state and the ld. Counsel of accused and have carefully perused the record. 
12. It is a cardinal principle of criminal jurisprudence that prosecution has to prove its case beyond reasonable doubts by leading reliable, cogent and convincing evidence. Further, it is a settled proposition of criminal law that in order to successfully bring home the guilt of the accused,
prosecution is supposed to stand on its own legs and it cannot derive any benefits whatsoever from the weakness, if any, in the defense of the accused. Accused is entitled to the benefit of every reasonable doubt in the prosecution story and any such doubt in the prosecution case entitles the accused to acquittal. 
13. PW 1, PW 2 & PW-3 who were the main witnesses have not identified the accused as the person who committed offence neither they have identified the offending vehicle. Prosecution has failed to establish the identity of accused and offending vehicle in present case. 
14. In such circumstances it cannot be said that prosecution has proved its case beyond reasonable doubt. Accordingly, accused Ajay Kumar S/o Chand Ram is acquitted for offence under section 279/304 A IPC.
